Every reporting rule of the two autoresearch loops on a harder bank: the donor-level regression with eSVD’s fitted library beats DESeq2, the fitted library matters when confounders vary within a donor, and the posterior’s floor on the library should go

Kevin Z. Lin (drafted by Claude)

2026-11-12

1 Overview

This document is built from the two autoresearch loops on the reported log fold change and its standard error (autoresearch_lfcse/, autoresearch_lfcse2/; their reports are notes/RUN_nov11_claude.md in each), from Kevin’s note of 2026-11-12 (2026-11-12_autoresearch_additional-exploration-beyond-score.txt), and from a new bank of simulated cohorts built for it, lfcse-bank-3. No new rule is proposed. Every rule the two loops considered is run again, as it was written, on a bank that is harder in the ways the note asks for, and is assessed on more than the score.

The question. Of the rules the two loops considered, which one should eSVD2 report the log2 fold change and SE from, once the bank has strong confounders, genes of very different sparsity, few or many true DEGs, and replicate cohorts, and once each rule is also compared head to head with DESeq2, run with library sizes other than eSVD’s, and checked against its own significance calls?

What the document argues:

  1. donor_wls beats pseudobulk DESeq2 on all three banks, by 0.252 nats per gene on the new bank, where it is the better of the two in 87% of cohorts (section 5).
  2. eSVD’s fitted library is worth having when a confounder varies within a donor, and only then. With cell-level confounders, donor_wls with the summed counts as library scores 1.058 against 0.453 with the fitted library; with donor-level confounders, however strong, the two are equal (sections 6 and 7).
  3. The posterior’s floor of 0.1 on the fitted library hurts the rule. For sparse genes the fitted library sits at the floor and carries no depth or covariate adjustment. Without the floor donor_wls gains 0.032 nats on the new bank and loses nothing elsewhere (section 7.3).
  4. Sparse genes are harder for every rule, and donor_wls attenuates the fold change of the sparsest ones: its slope on the truth is 0.87 for genes with over 95% zeros (section 8).
  5. True DEGs replicate and null genes do not, for every rule, and the replicate correlation of the null genes detects confounding a rule has left in (section 9).
  6. eSVD-DE’s own significance calls and the reported interval are two analyses. On the new bank 76% of the genes the package calls have a donor_wls@esvd_nofloor interval that leaves out zero, and the package’s calls have a false discovery proportion of 19% at a nominal 5% (section 10).
  7. The recommendation: report from donor_wls with the fitted library without its floor (donor_wls@esvd_nofloor); keep state_adjusted as the rule for the effect at fixed cell state, which is still a decision about the target and not about the rule (section 11).

How to read. Green boxes close each results section with what it changes; the blue box describes the new bank; grey boxes say which bank a section reads; the orange box in section 11 is the procedure. A reader of the boxes alone has the argument.

2 Definitions

2.1 Notation and the score

A cohort has cells \(c\) in donors \(d\), genes \(g\), counts \(A_{cg}\), an arm (case or control) per donor, and covariates. A reporting rule takes one fitted eSVD-DE cohort and returns, for every gene, a log2 fold change \(\widehat\beta_g\) and a standard error \(s_g\). The score of a cohort is the Gaussian negative log-likelihood of the true log2 fold change \(\beta_g\) under the reported pair, averaged over genes, in nats per gene: \[\frac{1}{p}\sum_g \left\{\tfrac12 \log(2\pi s_g^2) + \frac{(\widehat\beta_g - \beta_g)^2}{2 s_g^2}\right\}.\] Lower is better. It rewards an accurate fold change and an SE that is neither too small nor too large.

Two truths are used. The marginal truth is the log2 ratio of mean expression between the populations of case and control donors at equal covariates and depth; it includes any difference in cell state between the arms. The direct truth is the case-control effect at fixed cell state. They differ only where the arms differ in cell state (state = donor_arm of banks 2 and 3). eSVD-DE’s convention is the marginal one.

Two validity gates from the loops are reported beside the score. slope_weak is the slope of the reported logFC on the truth over weak-effect genes (below 0.5 in absolute value); the loops required \([0.9, 1.1]\), so that a rule cannot win by shrinking. se_strong is the SE of strong-effect genes over the SE of other genes of the same expression level; the second loop required \([0.92, 1.08]\), so that a rule cannot win by an SE that follows the estimated logFC.

2.2 The rules

Every rule is the file the loops left, unedited (autoresearch_lfcse2/candidates/, autoresearch_lfcse*/notes/RULE_*).

Name in the tables Rule Reads of the fit From
stored what 1.2.0 reports: log ratio of the arms’ mean posterior, SE from the posterior’s mixture variances posterior package
null_rescaled stored, the logFC shifted by the empirical null’s mean and the SE multiplied by its SD posterior, empirical null baseline of loop 2
deshrunk stored’s logFC; between-donor SE of the posterior donor means divided by the shrinkage weight posterior, library, nuisance rate reference
raw ratio of the arms’ means of donor means of \(A/\ell\), delta-method SE between donors library reference
raw_null raw with the empirical null’s shift and rescaling library baseline of loop 1
donor_wls weighted regression of \(\log\{(y_{dg} + 1/2)/L_{dg}\}\) on the arm and the donor-level covariates, residual variance moderated across genes, logFC shifted by the null’s mean library kept by loop 1
gap_trend as donor_wls with voom-style weights and a variance trend in a covariate that contains the between-arm gap library withdrawn in loop 1 (fails se_strong)
embed_prior donor_wls with the embedding’s predicted donor variance in the moderation prior library, embedding kept by loop 2, run A
state_adjusted donor_wls on summaries with the embedding’s donor offset removed; the arm coefficients’ component along the loadings subtracted library, embedding kept by loop 2, run B
deseq2 DESeq2 on donor pseudobulk; design: every covariate (cell-level ones as donor means) and the arm nothing comparator
deseq2_nocell the same without the cell-level covariates in the design nothing comparator

Here \(y_{dg}\) is the donor’s summed count and \(L_{dg}\) its summed library. The intermediate commits the loops discarded are not rerun.

2.3 The library variants

donor_wls, gap_trend, raw_null, embed_prior and state_adjusted read a cells \(\times\) genes library \(\ell_{cg}\). The fit’s is \(\ell_{cg} = \max\{\exp(z_g^\top C_c), 0.1\}\) over every covariate but the arm: the intercept, the log of the cell’s summed counts with a per-gene coefficient, and each other covariate with a per-gene coefficient. A variant is written rule@library.

Library What it is Design of the rule
(none) the fitted library as the posterior uses it, floored at 0.1 donor-level covariates
esvd_nofloor the fitted library without the floor donor-level covariates
esvd_depth the fitted intercept and depth coefficient only, no floor donor-level covariates
total the cell’s summed counts donor-level covariates
total_cov the cell’s summed counts donor-level covariates and the donor means of the cell-level ones
sf_cov summed counts rescaled so that a donor’s total is DESeq2’s median-of-ratios size factor of the pseudobulk as total_cov
tmm_cov summed counts times edgeR’s TMM factor of the donor’s pseudobulk as total_cov
oracle the generator’s library times the true effect of the cell-level covariates (bank 3 only) donor-level covariates

total_cov is what an analyst without eSVD would do: pseudobulk by donor, normalize by depth, and put each covariate in the design at the donor level.

3 The new bank

lfcse-bank-3 holds 216 examples. An example is one population (the gene-level truth: 600 genes with their intercepts, loadings, over-dispersion, case-control and covariate effects) and two replicate cohorts drawn from it with new donors and new cells, each fitted end to end by eSVD2 1.2.0 at rank 5 (432 fits). Counts follow the eSVD model, with donor effects as in the second bank. Eight factors vary:

  1. donors: 10, 20 or 40, half per arm.
  2. confound: sex and age are in every cohort. mild: per-gene effects of SD 0.2, nearly balanced between arms (sex 40% against 60%). donor: effects of SD 0.5, sex 20% of controls against 80% of cases, cases older by one SD. cell: the mild donor-level covariates plus two cell-level ones, Pct (continuous, per-gene effect SD 0.3, cases higher by 0.8 within-donor SD) and Phase (binary, per-gene effect SD 0.5, 20% of control cells against 50% of case cells). A DEG’s effect has SD 0.6, so at donor and cell the confounders move every gene by about as much as the arm moves the DEGs.
  3. deg: few (5% of genes with an effect, both signs, the others exactly null), many (30%, three in four positive, the others exactly null), dense (every gene nonzero, most weakly).
  4. state: none; donor (donor-level cell states of rank 3 carry three quarters of the donor variance); donor_arm (the same, and the arms differ in mean state, so the marginal and direct truths differ).
  5. cells: 50 per donor, or unequal (30 to 600).
  6. donor_sd: 0.2 or 0.5 on the log scale.
  7. arm_sd: equal donor variance in the arms, or three times larger in the cases.
  8. depth: none, or a donor-level shift of a block of 15% of the genes.

Gene intercepts are uniform on \((-4, 1.5)\) in every cohort, so each cohort holds genes with a mean of 0.02 counts per cell beside genes with a mean of 4. The 216 examples are a balanced one-sixth fraction of the 1296 combinations: every level and every pair of levels of two factors appears equally often. There is one split, because nothing is tuned on this bank.

Table 1. Genes by their share of zero counts in the three banks (test splits of banks 1 and 2), with the share of genes whose nuisance rate is capped or at the boundary, and the share of a gene’s cells whose fitted library is below the posterior’s floor of 0.1.

bank 1 80 to 95% 0%
bank 1 over 95% 0%

Every fit of the new bank succeeded (3 of 432 with a warning). On average 64% of a cohort’s counts are zero and 50% of its genes have a capped or boundary nuisance rate, against 73% on the Velmeshev cohort and 13% in the first bank. The first bank has almost no gene with more than half zeros; the new bank has 44% of its genes above 80%.

The last column of Table 1 is a finding of its own. The fitted library contains the gene’s intercept, so for a gene with under one count in ten cells it falls below 0.1 and the posterior sets it to 0.1 for every cell. For such a gene the “library” a rule reads is a constant: it has neither the depth nor the covariates in it. Section 7.3 measures what this costs.

The new bank covers what the note asks for: confounders as strong as the effect of interest at the donor level and at the cell level, genes from a few percent to 99% zeros within every cohort, 5% or 30% true DEGs among exact nulls, and a replicate cohort for every population. Building it exposed that the fitted library is constant for sparse genes because of the posterior’s floor.

Figure 1. Mean score of each rule on the new bank under the two truths, with one standard error. The dashed line is DESeq2 under the marginal truth.

The order of the rules carries over to the new bank. Under the marginal truth the donor-level regressions (donor_wls, embed_prior, gap_trend) lead on all three banks, the posterior-based rules (stored, null_rescaled, deshrunk) trail DESeq2, and raw_null sits between. Under the direct truth state_adjusted leads by 0.324 nats on the new bank, as it did on the second.

The gates. gap_trend fails se_strong again (1.15 on the new bank, 1.20 on the second): its lead in Table 2 is the SE following the estimated logFC, and it stays withdrawn. state_adjusted has a slope_weak of 0.51 under the marginal truth, by construction (it removes the arms’ difference in cell state), and 0.93 under the direct truth. Every other rule’s marginal slope_weak is between 0.87 and 0.92 on the new bank, DESeq2’s is 0.93: the bank’s sparse genes pull every rule’s slope down, and section 8 shows where.

Calibration. donor_wls covers the truth 92.3% of the time at a nominal 95% on the new bank (94.0% on the second, 95.0% on the first), and the SD of its z-statistic on exactly null genes is 1.09: its SE is a few percent too small here. stored is too wide (SD of z 0.85) and biased on null genes (median logFC -0.09); null_rescaled is too narrow (coverage 90.3%).

Failures. raw and raw_null return a non-finite value for 120 genes in 61 cohorts of the new bank (a gene with no count in one arm); they are scored on the remaining genes. No other rule failed on any cohort.

Nothing in the new bank reverses the loops’ ranking. Under the marginal truth the donor-level regression family is best on all three banks; under the direct truth state_adjusted is. gap_trend fails the same gate it failed before. The posterior-based rules, including what 1.2.0 stores, are behind DESeq2 on every bank.

Figure 2. Score minus DESeq2’s on the new bank (marginal truth), by level of each factor. Blue: the rule is better than DESeq2; red: worse. The colour scale is capped at 0.4 nats.

donor_wls beats DESeq2 on every bank and in every stratum of the new bank. The margin is 0.054 nats on the first bank, 0.062 on the second and 0.252 on the new one, each many paired standard errors from zero, and donor_wls is the better of the two in 99%, 90% and 87% of cohorts.

Where the margin comes from on the new bank. At confound = mild and donor the margin is 0.060 and 0.045, the size seen on the earlier banks. At confound = cell it is 0.652. There DESeq2 has to adjust for the cell-level covariates through their donor means, which are nearly collinear with the arm, and its RMSE goes to 1.18 log2 units against 0.48 for donor_wls. Leaving the cell-level covariates out of DESeq2’s design (deseq2_nocell) trades variance for bias: its score at confound = cell is 1.518 with a coverage of 76%, and donor_wls beats it there by 1.065 (SE 0.077).

The rules that do not beat DESeq2. stored, deshrunk, raw and null_rescaled are behind DESeq2 on every bank; raw_null is behind on banks 1 and 2 and ahead on the new bank only because of confound = cell.

The rule the first loop kept is more accurate than DESeq2 by the loops’ score on all three banks and in every stratum of the new one, and the margin is ten times larger when confounders vary within a donor. What 1.2.0 stores today is less accurate than DESeq2 on all three.

Donor-level confounders, however strong, are handled by any rule with the covariates in its donor-level design. From mild to donor every rule loses about the same amount (donor_wls 0.315 to 0.609, DESeq2 0.375 to 0.653): the price of an arm that is partly collinear with sex and age, paid in variance. The coverage holds. raw_null, which has no design and relies on the library to remove sex and age, keeps its coverage but loses more.

Cell-level confounders separate the rules. A rule that neither reads the covariates from the library nor has them in its design is biased: donor_wls@total and donor_wls@esvd_depth cover the truth 75% and 75% of the time. A rule with their donor means in its design is unbiased and noisy: donor_wls@total_cov has an RMSE of 1.06. A rule that reads the fitted library, in which each covariate was regressed out cell by cell with its per-gene coefficient, is close to the oracle: donor_wls 0.453, without the floor 0.392, oracle 0.331.

eSVD’s regressing-out of covariates is what makes the rule work when a confounder varies within a donor and differs between the arms: the within-donor variation identifies each gene’s coefficient, which a donor-level analysis cannot use. For confounders that are constant within a donor the fit’s adjustment adds nothing to a donor-level design.

Figure 3. donor_wls with each library on the new bank, by level of confound: score (left) and coverage of the 95% interval (right), marginal truth.

Without cell-level confounders the fitted library is barely better than the summed counts. The gain over total is 0.004 nats on the first bank and 0.016 on the second; on the new bank it is 0.001 at confound = mild and -0.010 at donor. The first loop’s margin over DESeq2 (0.054) is therefore the regression and its variance moderation, not the library: donor_wls@total keeps 0.050 of it on the first bank and 0.046 of 0.062 on the second. This answers the open question the first run left.

The size-factor estimates are the summed counts. DESeq2’s median of ratios and TMM change the score by under 0.001 nats against total_cov, on every bank.

With cell-level confounders the fitted library is worth 0.604 nats over the standard practice (total_cov) and 1.029 over the summed counts alone. esvd_depth, the fitted library without its covariates, is as bad as the summed counts: the whole gain is the covariates in the library, none of it the per-gene depth coefficient.

The pattern is donor_wls’s for every rule: a large gain from the fitted library at confound = cell, a small one or none elsewhere. raw_null depends on the fitted library most, because it has no design of its own and the library is its only adjustment for any covariate.

7.3 The posterior’s floor on the library

Table 8. Score of donor_wls on the new bank with the fitted library as the posterior floors it, without the floor, and with the oracle library, by the gene’s share of zeros (marginal truth); the last four columns at confound = mild and cell.
Share of zeros Cells at the floor donor_wls donor_wls@esvd_nofloor donor_wls@oracle donor_wls, mild donor_wls@esvd_nofloor, mild donor_wls, cell donor_wls@esvd_nofloor, cell
under 50% 0% 0.153 0.135 0.151 0.036 0.017 0.096 0.076
50 to 80% 3% 0.326 0.309 0.313 0.190 0.174 0.271 0.258
80 to 95% 49% 0.657 0.588 0.570 0.474 0.443 0.699 0.562
over 95% 97% 0.929 0.908 0.831 0.752 0.758 1.022 0.936

compute_posterior() sets every fitted library below library_min = 0.1 to 0.1, and every rule of the loops read the library after that step. For a gene with 80 to 95% zeros about half of the cells are at the floor; above 95% nearly all are (Table 8). Removing the floor improves donor_wls by 0.032 nats on the new bank (paired SE 0.003, better in 81% of cohorts) and by 0.007 on the second bank (SE 0.001); on the first bank, which has no sparse gene, it changes nothing. The gain is largest at confound = cell, where the floored genes lose their covariate adjustment, and it also improves state_adjusted under the direct truth by 0.034 (SE 0.003). Without the floor donor_wls is within 0.011 nats of the oracle library on the new bank.

This is a change to which library the rule reads, not a new rule: the formula of donor_wls is untouched.

The summed counts, or any standard size factor, are as effective as eSVD’s library unless a confounder varies within donors; when one does, the fitted library is worth half a nat per gene over the standard practice, and all of that comes from the covariates in it. The rule should read the fitted library before the posterior’s floor at 0.1, which otherwise discards the adjustment for sparse genes.

Figure 4. Score on the new bank by the gene’s share of zero counts (marginal truth). Every rule degrades with sparsity; the order of the rules changes for the posterior-based ones.

Every rule degrades with sparsity, and donor_wls stays ahead of DESeq2 in every bin: by 0.290 nats for genes under 50% zeros and by 0.310 for genes over 95%.

The posterior-based rules break at both ends. stored’s interval covers 100% of the sparsest genes and 89% of the densest: its SE is dominated by the within-cell term, which is far too large for a sparse gene. null_rescaled multiplies every gene’s SE by one factor and so covers 77% of the dense genes.

donor_wls attenuates the sparsest genes. For genes over 95% zeros its slope on the truth is 0.87 (DESeq2: 1.02). The half count added to a donor’s summed count before the logarithm pulls the donor means together when a donor has a handful of counts. The attenuation is absent below 95% zeros (1.00 at 80 to 95%). It explains the marginal slope_weak of 0.90 in Table 3, which sits at the edge of the loops’ gate; on genes under 95% zeros the rule is inside it.

The number of true DEGs moves the scores little. donor_wls scores 0.452 with 5% DEGs and 0.478 with 30% mostly upregulated, where every total-count library is shifted by the DEGs and the empirical null’s mean has to remove the shift. The median logFC of exactly null genes stays at -0.045 at many (stored: -0.159).

The ranking of the rules is the same for dense and sparse genes and for few and many DEGs. Two things are specific to sparse genes: the posterior-based SE is several times too large for them, and donor_wls shrinks the fold change of genes with over 95% zeros by about 13%. Genes that sparse are usually filtered before a DE analysis; the SE and the logFC reported for them should be read with that in mind.

True DEGs replicate and null genes do not, as expected, for every rule. For donor_wls@esvd_nofloor the median correlation between replicates is 0.79 over the true DEGs and 0.00 over the null genes, whose logFC is centred at -0.015. The logFC that 1.2.0 stores (stored) replicates as well over the DEGs (0.78) but its null genes are centred at -0.10: the depth bias the empirical null’s mean removes in the other rules.

The DEGs replicate better under the eSVD-library rules than under DESeq2 (0.72), and much better with cell-level confounders (0.79 against 0.43), where DESeq2’s logFC is noisy.

A positive correlation among null genes is a detector of confounding left in. The replicates share the genes’ covariate coefficients, so whatever a rule fails to remove is the same in both. At confound = cell the null genes of donor_wls (floored library) correlate at 0.10 and those of donor_wls@esvd_nofloor at -0.01: the floor leaves the cell-level covariates in the sparse genes. At confound = donor, raw_null, which has no design, reaches 0.36.

At state = donor_arm the “null” genes replicate under every rule but state_adjusted (0.25 for donor_wls@esvd_nofloor, 0.06 for state_adjusted). This is not an error: the arms differ in cell state in the population, so those genes have a real marginal effect, and it replicates. It is the fork between the two targets seen from the replicates’ side.

Sparse DEGs replicate less (Table 14): the correlation falls from about 0.9 under 50% zeros to about 0.6 over 95%, for every rule.

The picture Kevin expected holds for every rule: true DEGs fall on the diagonal between replicates and null genes form a centred cloud. The replicate correlation of null genes is zero only when the rule has removed the confounders, which makes it a diagnostic one could compute on real replicate cohorts; it is how the floored library’s leftover confounding shows up without the truth.

10 Significant genes against the interval

All three banks, pooled over cohorts. Two tests call genes at FDR 5%: eSVD-DE’s test (the p-value 1.2.0 computes from the posterior-based Welch statistic and the empirical null, with BH; the same calls for every rule) and the rule’s own Wald test (\(\widehat\beta_g / s_g\) against a standard normal, with BH; DESeq2’s adjusted p-value for DESeq2). The interval is \(\widehat\beta_g \pm 2 s_g\).

What the question asks. Of the genes eSVD-DE’s test calls, the interval of the logFC that 1.2.0 stores leaves out zero for 75% on the new bank (64% on the second, 62% on the first). On the Velmeshev cohort the same number was 13%. For donor_wls@esvd_nofloor it is 76% on the new bank and 99% on the first. null_rescaled gives 100% by construction: its z-statistic is the test’s.

A rule’s own Wald test agrees with its interval by construction: a gene called by BH at 5% has \(|z| > 1.96\) at least, and on the new bank at least 100.0% of the genes a rule calls have \(|z| > 2\), for every rule. The disagreement in Table 15 is entirely between two analyses: the package’s test, built on the posterior, and the reported pair, built on donor-level summaries.

Where the two disagree, the package’s test is the less calibrated of the two. Its false discovery proportion at a nominal 5% is 19% over the new bank and 49% at deg = few (18% on the second bank, 8% on the first). The Wald test of donor_wls@esvd_nofloor has 4.8% (9.5% at few) with more power (9.7% against 7.2%), and DESeq2 5.4% (15.8% at few).

On the first bank the genes eSVD-DE calls and the donor_wls interval agree (99%). On the second and the new bank 14% and 24% of the called genes have an interval that covers zero, and there the package’s test has three to four times its nominal false discovery proportion while the Wald test of the reported pair is near nominal. If the reported pair comes from donor_wls, the p-value should come from the same pair, or the two will keep contradicting each other in the output table.

11 Recommendation

Report the log2 fold change and its SE from donor_wls, reading the fitted library before the posterior’s floor (donor_wls@esvd_nofloor). This is a consequence of the evidence under the marginal truth, eSVD-DE’s current convention:

  • under the marginal truth it is the best valid rule on the new bank, within 0.001 nats of the best on the second and within 0.004 on the first (Table 2; gap_trend scores slightly better and fails se_strong on every bank);
  • it beats DESeq2 in 94% of the new bank’s cohorts and in every stratum (Table 4, Figure 2);
  • it is within 0.011 nats of the same rule with the true library;
  • its Wald test has a false discovery proportion near the nominal 5% (4.8% on the new bank, 9.5% with few DEGs) where the package’s test has 19% (Table 16).

It uses the eSVD fit for one thing, the covariate-adjusted library, and section 6 shows that this is the one thing a donor-level analysis cannot do for itself when a confounder varies within donors. Without such a confounder the rule works as well with summed counts.

embed_prior is donor_wls under the marginal truth, to within 0.005 nats on every bank, and adds nothing.

state_adjusted remains the rule for the effect at fixed cell state, and that is a choice of target. Under the direct truth it leads by 0.324 nats on the new bank. Under the marginal truth it is also the best rule where donors have cell states that do not differ between the arms (state = donor: 0.171 against 0.455), slightly better at state = none (0.429 against 0.465), and wrong where the arms differ in state (0.996 against 0.456). The new bank does not test the two things its report flagged (an effect aligned with the loadings; a rank near the donor count), so it is not the default.

  1. Fit eSVD-DE as now (eSVD() or the stage-by-stage pipeline) with every covariate in the design, cell-level ones included.
  2. Form the library \(\ell_{cg} = \exp(z_g^\top C_c)\) over every covariate but the arm, without the floor at 0.1.
  3. Run donor_wls (autoresearch_lfcse/notes/RULE_nov11_claude.R) on the counts, the design, the donor labels and that library. It returns the log2 fold change and SE per gene.
  4. Report, beside the pair, the Wald z and its BH-adjusted p-value from the same pair, so that the significance call and the interval cannot disagree.
  5. Flag genes with over 95% zero counts: their fold change is attenuated by about 13% and their SE is the least reliable.
  6. Check on replicate or split cohorts, when available, that the logFC of presumed-null genes does not correlate between them; a positive correlation means a confounder is left in.
  7. Replacement: when the question is the effect at fixed cell state, run state_adjusted (autoresearch_lfcse2/notes/RULE_nov11_direct_claude.R) with the same library, after the two checks of its report.

Whether step 4 replaces the package’s posterior-based test is Kevin’s decision; the evidence here is that the posterior-based test has an inflated false discovery proportion on the second and third banks.

12 What we glossed over

  • The banks are simulated from the eSVD model. The fitted library’s advantage at confound = cell assumes the covariates act log-linearly with one coefficient per gene, which is the model the fit assumes. A real-cohort check is the replicate diagnostic of section 9.
  • The cell-level confounders are strongly unbalanced between arms (0.8 SD in Pct, 20% against 50% in Phase). The size of the gain over total_cov and DESeq2 depends on that imbalance; with a balanced cell-level covariate a donor-level analysis loses precision, not validity.
  • DESeq2 is run one way: pseudobulk by donor, default DESeq() and results(), with (deseq2) or without (deseq2_nocell) the donor means of cell-level covariates. No shrunken fold change, no cell-level model (NEBULA, MAST), no limma-voom or dreamlet.
  • The half count of donor_wls is what attenuates the sparsest genes (section 8). Changing it would be a new rule and was not tried.
  • donor_wls’s SE is a few percent too small on the new bank (coverage 92.8%, lower at confound = cell). The cell-level adjustment is estimated and its uncertainty is not in the SE.
  • The first bank’s cohort pairs have different true effects by design, so only the new bank supplies replicates.
  • Rank and effects aligned with the loadings are still not bank factors (open item of the second loop’s report).
  • The intermediate commits of the loops (38 and 19 experiments) were not rerun; only the reference rows and the kept rules were.
  • The floor exists for the posterior, where a tiny library makes the Gamma-Poisson update unstable. This document shows only that the reporting rule should not inherit it; whether the posterior’s own floor should change is a separate question.
